title: Sum of Perfect Square Ancestors
summary: Given an integer n and a tree with n nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, represented by edges, and an array nums assigning a positive integer to each node, calculate the sum of ti values for nodes 1 to n-1.
statement: Given an integer n and a tree with n nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, represented by edges, and an array nums assigning a positive integer to each node, calculate the sum of ti values for nodes 1 to n-1. ti is the count of ancestors of node i where the product of nums[i] and nums[ancestor] is a perfect square.
constraints: The rooted tree has up to 100,000 nodes, root zero, and n-1 undirected edges.
Each node value is between one and 100,000.
Count ancestor–descendant pairs whose value product is a perfect square.
target_time_complexity: O(V log log V + n log V)
hints: A product is a square exactly when both values have the same square-free kernel.
Factor every value by prime-exponent parity, then count equal kernels along the current root-to-node path.
An iterative DFS adds the current kernel on entry and removes it on exit; the prior count is this node’s matching ancestors.
The active counter contains exactly and only ancestors, while kernel equality is equivalent to every product prime exponent being even.
editorial: The active counter contains exactly and only ancestors, while kernel equality is equivalent to every product prime exponent being even.

tests.explanation: All three ancestor pairs have products 16 or 4, so the sum is three.
Nodes two and three each match root zero, giving two pairs.
